name: security-android-app-link-verification-review
intent: Android App Links domain verification and sensitive link routing
artifacts: Manifest intent filters, assetlinks ownership, installed package/signature and actual link consumer.
trace: Trace verified domain/path matching into application actions, keeping OS routing and in-app parameter authorization distinct.
experiment: Use owned test domains/emulators and an inert account fixture; compare intended verified link and an unverified/domain-mismatched link.
disproof: An intent filter or failed verification alone is not account takeover; establish a reachable protected consumer.
repair: Bind verified origins and in-app action policy, retesting intended links and rejected untrusted routing.
branch_decisions: Use the installed package signing certificate and actual OS domain-verification state, not manifest intent alone. Verified HTTPS links and custom schemes have different routing guarantees. A link reaching the intended app still requires transaction/resource authorization; failed verification does not prove an attacker app receives sensitive data under the tested user defaults.
operational_method: On Android11/API30 and lower, default App Links verification depends on matching Digital Asset Links for all declared hosts. Android12 introduced the updated verifier/per-host state; record actual OS, target/compat state and user routing choices. For an owned installed app, collect pm get-app-links or DomainVerificationManager state on supported versions, signing certificate and the actual delivered URL/consumer. A user-selected association differs from a domain-verified state, and a manifest or failed verification alone does not prove another app received protected data.
